documents: Humberston, J. L., & Lippmann, T. C. (2022). The effect of regional winds on subtidal along-inlet currents at Oregon Inlet, NC. JGR Oceans 127, e2022JC018513 (published PDF, 14 pages)

entry.evidence: This study tests the hypothesis that wind processes may be a first-order control of water level variations within a tidal inlet.

steps.action: Authors take from other inlet studies (Orescanin 2014, Wargula 2014) that wave forcing is small relative to pressure gradients well inside the inlet channel.
steps.quote: the influence of waves and inertia on the main inlet channel currents well inland of the ebb shoals and wave breaking was small

steps.action: Authors cite earlier speculation and qualitative reports that wind forcing causes flow anomalies at Oregon Inlet.
steps.quote: Jarrett (1978) speculated that anomalies observed in the flow through the inlet were due to wind forcing.

steps.action: Authors pose the open question of how much winds contribute to inlet hydrodynamics and by what mechanism.
steps.quote: neither the relative contributions of winds nor the primary mechanism of their influence has been well constrained [...]

steps.action: Authors state the hypothesis that winds are a first-order control of water level variations within the inlet.
steps.quote: This study tests the hypothesis that wind processes may be a first-order control of water level variations within a tidal inlet.

steps.action: Authors run a 40-day field experiment at Oregon Inlet in spring 2019, during which natural frontal wind events occur, and start it with a topo-bathymetric survey and a 10 m DEM.
steps.quote: A field experiment was conducted over a 40-day period from 7 March to 16 April 2019 at Oregon Inlet, NC.

steps.action: Authors use the DEM to place two bottom-mounted tripods (sound-side AWAC, ocean-side ADCP) 3.18 km apart so the along-channel water level gradient and current can be measured.
steps.quote: The DEM was used to guide the placement of two instrumented bottom-mounted tripods

steps.action: Authors reference sensor elevations to MSL against NOAA tide gauges, track tripod tilt (1-3 cm elevation error), and bound density-assumption errors from salinity and temperature variation (<1 cm).
steps.quote: Errors in the sea surface elevation owing to spatial and vertical deviations of 5 psu and 5°C from the mean salinity

steps.action: Authors record water levels, depth-integrated currents along the 8° principal flow axis, NOAA station winds, and wave heights from three sources, all on a common 15-min time vector.
steps.quote: There were strong multi-day variations in wind speed (ranging 0–10 m/s) and direction, including rapid wind reversals

steps.action: Authors fit and remove the astronomical tide with T_TIDE harmonic analysis, then apply a 33-hr pl66tn low-pass filter to isolate the subtidal water level, current, and wind.
steps.quote: The water level and current time series were subjected to a tidal analysis (using T_TIDE; Pawlowicz et al., 2002)

steps.action: Authors establish that the subtidal current exceeds the tidal current 45% of the time and is at least half as strong 70% of the time, so a non-tidal process is real.
steps.quote: [...] from these results alone that there is a non-tidal process with a consistent first-order influence on the currents at Oregon Inlet.

steps.action: Authors cross-correlate subtidal wind, subtidal water level gradient (STWL), and subtidal current (R = 0.88, 0.92, 0.96).
steps.quote: subtidal winds are in-phase and strongly coupled to both the STWL gradient (R = 0.88 at zero lag)

steps.action: Authors name rival forcings: local surface wind stress, a regional wind-induced setup/setdown pressure gradient, and wave momentum, and note that correlations alone cannot separate them.
steps.quote: Winds may force currents directly from local surface wind stress (Janzen & Wong, 1998) or indirectly from regional wind fields

steps.action: Authors formulate a 2-D steady subtidal momentum balance (pressure gradient, wind stress, radiation-stress wave forcing, quadratic bed drag), using drag and roughness values taken from the literature.
steps.quote: a simple 2-D steady force balance is considered

steps.action: Authors check the Spotter buoy wave record, used for the radiation stress gradient, against the offshore NDBC buoy that fills its gaps.
steps.quote: Figure 2e and correlation analysis indicate these two signals are very similar during times when they were both active

steps.action: Authors compare subtidal currents predicted three ways (pressure gradient only; plus wind drag; plus waves) with the observed current.
steps.quote: captures most of the variability of the ST current (R = 0.92, accounting for 83% of the variance)

steps.action: Authors rule out local wind drag and wave forcing as primary drivers; they find both are minor except during major wave events.
steps.quote: [...] was found to be a minor contribution to the net ST current.

steps.action: Authors attribute the model's overprediction of flood and underprediction of ebb to the ADCP's location in the ebb-dominated channel, not to the force balance.
steps.quote: This is perhaps partly due to the current observations being collected within main ebb channel on the ocean side

steps.action: Authors examine two natural storm events: on 26-31 March wind and wave forcing are aligned; on 10-16 April southerly winds oppose the wave forcing.
steps.quote: the passage of a storm event between 10 and 16 April produced 3 m significant wave heights driven by winds out of the south

steps.action: Authors reject waves as the driver of the STWL gradient, because the pressure forcing followed the wind even when it opposed the wave forcing.
steps.quote: consistent with the hypothesis that winds, not waves, are setting up the STWL gradient that drives the along-channel current.

steps.action: Authors compare NOAA astronomical-only water level predictions and T_TIDE current predictions with observations (RMSE 0.23-0.25 m; 0.64 m/s during the March event).
steps.quote: the predicted water levels based solely on astronomical forces had a root mean square error

steps.action: Authors fit a linear regression of the STWL gradient on along-channel subtidal wind (R2 = 0.75) as a simple empirical predictor.
steps.quote: the STWL gradient through the inlet increases in magnitude by 3.6 cm/km for every 5 m/s positive increase in the wind speed

steps.action: Authors compare currents predicted from tides plus the wind-derived STWL gradient with tides alone (R2 0.84 versus 0.52).
steps.quote: This simple empirical model improved the explained variance of the observed currents

steps.action: Authors raise new questions on how wind forcing fits the tide-wave inlet morphology classification and whether wind seasonality adds a seasonal signal.
steps.quote: Do wind effects cause the system to behave like one with a larger tidal range, a smaller one, or in some entirely new way?

steps.action: Authors keep the claim that regional winds, through a setup/setdown pressure gradient, exert first-order control on subtidal currents at Oregon Inlet.
steps.quote: These findings provide evidence that regional winds exert a first order influence on tidal inlet hydrodynamics at Oregon Inlet.

tree.answer: Subtidal non-tidal currents at Oregon Inlet, rivaling the tides 45% of the time
Winds, water levels and currents are observed directly; the forcing contributions are not
Test whether winds are a first-order control and by which mechanism
Local wind stress, regional wind setup/setdown pressure gradient, wave forcing
Partly; the rivals are usually in phase, so they are separated by force-balance terms and by an event where wind and waves oppose
Found, in a 40-day field deployment with natural frontal wind events

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Several wind events in 40 days; a linear wind-gradient regularity is fitted
Only instrument premise checks and one opposing-forcing event; no parameter sensitivity and no other site
Wind-induced pressure gradient is dominant; waves and local wind stress are lower order

end.claim: Regional winds set up a subtidal water level gradient through Oregon Inlet that forces along-channel subtidal currents comparable to the tidal currents, with wave forcing and local wind drag of lower order.

decisive_move.sentence: Without the force-balance comparison, which shows that the measured wind-induced pressure gradient alone reproduces 83% of the subtidal current variance, the attribution to regional winds rather than local wind stress or waves would rest on correlation only.

gates.evidence: The stated wind hypothesis (p. 3) shaped the measurement of the along-channel gradient between two tripods placed from the DEM (p. 4), but the deployment was a general-purpose field experiment. The force balance could have failed to reproduce the currents, and the April event could have shown wave-aligned forcing (p. 9). The setup/setdown mechanism itself is inferred 'in combination with findings from previous studies' (p. 1), not measured. No preregistration; drag coefficients were taken from the literature, not fixed against held-out data.

imports.item: time-lagged cross-correlation, low-pass filtering and linear regression
acoustic Doppler current profilers (Nortek AWAC, RDI Workhorse)

novelty_claims.quote: The strong correlation between winds and the STWL gradient measured through the mouth of Oregon Inlet provides new
implying that winds may play an underappreciated role in tidal inlet dynamics

limits: Single inlet, a single 40-day spring deployment, and one ADCP in the ebb channel. The regional setup/setdown mechanism is inferred from the inlet gradient plus prior studies; water levels on either side of the barrier chain were not measured here. The force balance uses literature values (Cd = 0.005 from New River Inlet, z0 = 2 m, fr = 2.5) with no reported sensitivity test. Wave forcing is estimated from a buoy seaward of the ebb delta, which the authors say overestimates it. Inference: because the pressure term uses the measured gradient, the force-balance fit partly restates the gradient-current correlation. The empirical regression and the 32% skill gain are in-sample, with no held-out period. Wind range is given as 0–18 m/s in the abstract and 0–10 m/s in the text. Sub-claims: ST current exceeds the tidal current 45% of the time (estimate_with_resolution, without uncertainty); linear STWL-wind relation, R2 = 0.75 (regularity_in_range, range not stated). No review file was supplied, so the review process is not visible; the acknowledgments say the reviewers 'significantly improved the manuscript'.

disagreements.target: Traditional tidal inlet classification based on tidal range and wave climate (Hayes, 1975, 1980)
disagreements.support: Wind-driven subtidal currents rival the tides at an inlet that the delta ratio classifies as wave dominated, so a scheme of tides and waves alone misses a first-order forcing.
disagreements.quote: cause irregular hydrodynamic patterns not well described by the traditional inlet classification scheme.

disagreements.target: Applied tidal forecasting, NOAA Tides and Currents predictions near Oregon Inlet
disagreements.support: Astronomical-only predictions had a water level RMSE of 0.23-0.25 m and a current RMSE of 0.64 m/s during the March storm; adding the wind-derived gradient raised R2 from 0.52 to 0.84.
disagreements.quote: likely one of the reasons they are poorly constrained (or ignored) within applied forecasting efforts

alternatives_considered.alternatives: pressure gradient only; pressure gradient plus local wind shear; pressure gradient plus wind shear plus wave forcing
alternatives_considered.reason: to separate the contributions of regional wind setup, local wind stress and waves

alternatives_considered.chosen: Radiation stress from the Spotter buoy seaward of the ebb delta, with gaps filled from the NDBC buoy
alternatives_considered.alternatives: wave data at the ocean-side ADCP
alternatives_considered.reason: wave data were not preserved at the ocean-side ADCP

alternatives_considered.chosen: Ignore the cross-channel current in the bed drag
alternatives_considered.reason: on average it is 6% of the along-channel current

alternatives_considered.chosen: Treat barometric pressure as negligible in the along-channel slope
alternatives_considered.reason: atmospheric pressure gradients act over much larger horizontal scales than the inlet

alternatives_considered.chosen: Constant density of 1,025 kg/m3 for the pressure-to-water-level conversion
alternatives_considered.alternatives: spatially and vertically varying salinity and temperature
alternatives_considered.reason: well-mixed, unstratified inlet with limited freshwater input

alternatives_considered.alternatives: numerical model with broad coverage and tuned boundary conditions
alternatives_considered.reason: may suffice for the practical purpose of operational forecasts
